cards.card_text: At harvest time, God says don't reap to the very edges of the field or gather the gleanings, and don't strip the vineyard bare or pick up the fallen grapes.
cards.verse_text: When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.
cards.snippet: …to reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.

cards.card_text: Then, right in the middle of the feasts, God gives a harvest rule: don't reap all the way to the edges of the field, and don't gather the gleanings.
cards.verse_text: When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap all the way to the edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.
cards.snippet: …all the way to the edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.

cards.card_text: God tells Israel to leave the edges of the field and the gleanings of the harvest.
cards.verse_text: When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap all the way to the edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.
cards.snippet: …all the way to the edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.

cards.card_text: Instead, with angry men in his face, he asks them a question about GRAPES: aren't the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer, his own clan (Judges 6:11)?
cards.verse_text: Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?
cards.snippet: Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?

cards.card_text: True or false: After the reaping, the LORD says gleanings will still remain.
cards.verse_text: Yet gleanings will remain, like an olive tree that has been beaten—two or three berries atop the tree, four or five on its fruitful branches,” declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
cards.snippet: Yet gleanings will remain, like an olive tree that has been beaten—two or three…

cards.card_text: Then the LORD asks two questions: wouldn't grape gatherers leave some gleanings, and wouldn't thieves in the night steal only what they wanted?
cards.verse_text: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings?
cards.snippet: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings?

cards.card_text: If thieves came by night, wouldn't they steal only what they wanted, and if grape gatherers came, wouldn't they leave some gleanings?
cards.verse_text: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings?
cards.snippet: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings?

cards.card_text: Now the prophet Micah speaks for himself, and he opens with "Woe is me!" He says he's like someone gathering summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard, after the harvest is done.
cards.verse_text: For I am like one gathering summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster to eat, no early fig that I crave.
cards.snippet: For I am like one gathering summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster to eat, no early fig…

cards.card_text: Micah compares himself to someone gleaning a vineyard after the harvest.
cards.verse_text: For I am like one gathering summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster to eat, no early fig that I crave.
cards.snippet: For I am like one gathering summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster to eat, no early fig…
